title: Episode 181: The C++0x Concepts Story with Doug Gregor (Part 2)

sentences.en: I certainly agree with you that given all of the time that was spent on concepts, what we got, I think, is a little is unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 我完全同意你的看法，考虑到我们在概念上花了很多时间，最后得到的东西，我觉得，多多少少有点遗憾。

sentences.en: I was rereading the 2003 paper to see what our goals were.
sentences.zh: 我在重新阅读2003年的那篇论文，看看我们当时的目标是什么。

sentences.en: And separate type checking is the one goal.
sentences.zh: 而独立类型检查就是其中一个目标。

sentences.en: That is the one thing that if we had it, you could even throw out concept maps.
sentences.zh: 那是唯一的一点，如果我们拥有它，你甚至可以把概念映射（concept maps）扔掉。

sentences.en: If you had separate type checking, it would have made generic programming in C++ an order of magnitude easier, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你有了独立类型检查，它会让C++中的泛型编程变得简单一个数量级，对吧？

sentences.en: It would no longer be the domain of experts to use templates and use them well.
sentences.zh: 使用模板以及用好模板将不再是专家们的专利领域。

sentences.en: It would be something that every programmer just does because they need the abstraction.
sentences.zh: 它会变成每个程序员都在做的事情，因为他们需要这种抽象。

sentences.en: Welcome to ADSB The Podcast, episode 181, recorded on April 29th, 2024.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听 ADSB 播客第 181 期，录制于 2024 年 4 月 29 日。

sentences.en: My name is Connor.
sentences.zh: 我的名字是康纳（Connor）。

sentences.en: And today with my co-host, Bryce, we continue our chat with Doug Greger from Apple about the history of C++ OX concepts.
sentences.zh: 今天我的联合主持人是布莱斯（Bryce），我们将继续与来自苹果公司的道格·格雷格（Doug Greger）畅谈 C++0x 概念的历史。

sentences.en: So Joe Coder killed C++ OX concepts.
sentences.zh: 所以说，是虚构的“小明程序员”（Joe Coder）扼杀 了 C++0x 概念。

sentences.en: I think projections of the thinking onto a mythical Joe Coder is the main thing here.
sentences.zh: 我认为，把各种想法投射到一个虚构的小明程序员身上，才是这里的主要问题。

sentences.en: There were other complaints.
sentences.zh: 当时还有其他一些抱怨。

sentences.en: So there was concern about the compile time performance of the concept GCC prototype because it was doing all this template definition checking for the algorithm setter.
sentences.zh: 比如有人担心概念 GCC 原型的编译时间性能，因为它为算法设置做了所有这些模板定义检查。

sentences.en: But there's always going to be some compile time.
sentences.zh: 但编译时间总是不可避免的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's a compile time cost to C++ 20 concepts.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，C++20 概念本身也是有编译时间成本的。

sentences.en: People have done a bunch more time.
sentences.zh: 人们花了更多的时间在上面。

sentences.en: There's always going to be some compile time cost to checking versus not checking, right?
sentences.zh: 检查与不检查相比，总归是会有一些编译时间成本的，对吧？

sentences.en: I fully agree with you.
sentences.zh: 我完全赞同你的观点。

sentences.en: It seemed like a strange complaint.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是一个奇怪的抱怨。

sentences.en: It hadn't come up before.
sentences.zh: 之前从未出现过。

sentences.en: It hasn't come after.
sentences.zh: 之后也没有出现过。

sentences.en: I recall hearing some, I think, not particularly well substantiated concerns or claims of that
sentences.zh: 我记得曾听到过一些我认为并不是特别有充分根据的担忧或说法，即

sentences.en: the, not about the compile time performance of the type checking or the definition checking,
sentences.zh: 关于类型检查或定义检查的编译时间性能，

sentences.en: but that it was somehow an insolvable problem that the definition checking could not be done.
sentences.zh: 而是说这在某种程度上是一个无法解决的问题，定义检查根本无法完成。

sentences.en: And that that was why C++ OX concepts did not succeed.
sentences.zh: 而这正是 C++0x 概念未能成功的原因。

sentences.en: So it depends on whether you demand perfect checking or not.
sentences.zh: 所以这取决于你是否要求完美的检查。

sentences.en: So if we walk back a little bit to what separate type checking means, you are type checking the implementation of a template against the constraints that it states.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果我们回顾一下独立类型检查的含义，你是在根据模板声明的约束条件来对模板的实现进行类型检查。

sentences.en: Now, C++ has all sorts of ways in which you can make a template behave differently.
sentences.zh: 现在，C++ 有各种各样的方法可以让你使模板表现得不同。

sentences.en: So imagine, for example, my template definition, you know, over some template type parameter
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，举个例子，我的模板定义，你知道的，针对某个模板类型参数

sentences.en: T uses a vector of T.
sentences.zh: T 使用了 T 的向量（vector）。

sentences.en: Now what happens when T becomes bool?
sentences.zh: 现在，当 T 变成 bool 时会发生什么？

sentences.en: You've kicked over to the partial specialization of vector.
sentences.zh: 你已经切换到了 vector 的偏特化版本。

sentences.en: The partial specialization of vector could be completely unrelated to the generic primary template for vector.
sentences.zh: vector 的偏特化版本可能与 vector 的通用主模板完全无关。

sentences.en: And so if you have a language that has something like partial specialization or where you want
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你使用的语言具有偏特化之类的特性，或者你希望

sentences.en: to be able to do overloading in sort of an ad hoc manner at template instantiation time,
sentences.zh: 在模板实例化时以一种特设（ad hoc）的方式进行重载，

sentences.en: you cannot actually fully type check a template definition and be certain it's going to work
sentences.zh: 你实际上无法完全对模板定义进行类型检查，也无法确信它能在所有情况下都能工作，

sentences.en: in all cases because someone can just drop in an explicit specialization or a partial specialization of one of the types of template types it uses and things can break.
sentences.zh: 因为别人可以随时加入它所使用的其中一个模板类型的显式特化或偏特化，然后事情就会崩溃。

sentences.en: So C++ OX concepts were able to do template definition checking using the primary templates and
sentences.zh: 所以 C++0x 概念能够利用主模板进行模板定义检查，并

sentences.en: doing overload resolution essentially based on what knowledge it has of the template arguments and their capabilities.
sentences.zh: 基本上根据它对模板参数及其功能的了解来进行重载决议。

sentences.en: Now, throughout the C++ OX concepts process, we actually loosened the constraints on template instantiations a little bit.
sentences.zh: 在整个 C++0x 概念的发展过程中，我们实际上稍微放松了对模板实例化的约束。

sentences.en: So this is a deliberate decision in reaction to move semantics, actually, the addition to move semantics into the language where the original definition of C++ OX concepts would
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个刻意的决定，其实是为了应对移动语义（move semantics）的加入，即在语言中加入移动语义时，C++0x 概念的最初定义会

sentences.en: say when you pick an overload at template definition time for any operation, that is the overload that you use at instantiation time no matter what.
sentences.zh: 声明：当你在模板定义时为任何操作选择重载时，无论如何，这就是你在实例化时使用的重载。

sentences.en: The change we made is that we redo overload resolution with the actual template arguments types that come in, the concrete ones at instantiation time.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的改变是，我们用进来的实际模板参数类型（即实例化时的具体类型）重新进行重载决议。

sentences.en: This is treated as a performance optimization because it meant, for example, that if you're passing
sentences.zh: 这被视为一种性能优化，因为这意味着，例如，如果你在这里传递

sentences.en: an R value here and an L value here, you could pick up an overload that took an R value on the
sentences.zh: 一个右值（Rvalue），在那里传递一个左值（Lvalue），你可以挑选出一个

sentences.en: right side and an L value on the left side, and that would have better performance than if you always pushed it through the const L value path.
sentences.zh: 右侧接受右值、左侧接受左值的重载，这会比总是走 const 左值路径具有更好的性能。

sentences.en: We can cite that for you in the show notes to see the decisions.
sentences.zh: 我们可以在节目shownotes中为你列出这些引文，以便查看这些决策。

sentences.en: But that's a very explicit, we gave up some of the separate type checking to maintain the
sentences.zh: 但这是一个非常明确的做法：我们放弃了一部分独立类型检查，以维护

sentences.en: C++ performance model.
sentences.zh: C++ 的性能模型。

sentences.en: And so it's true that you don't have perfection, but this kind of overloading is pretty rare, and it's pretty rare that it actually breaks anything.
sentences.zh: 所以确实，你无法做到完美，但这种重载相当罕见，而且它真正破坏任何东西的情况也非常少见。

sentences.en: So you still had the property that you had almost no instantiation time failures.
sentences.zh: 因此你依然具备这样的特性：几乎不存在实例化时的失败。

sentences.en: They only really came in when you're doing funny overloading or partial specializations that don't line up with the primary templates.
sentences.zh: 它们真正出现的时候，只有在你做了奇怪的重载，或者偏特化与主模板不匹配的时候。

sentences.en: So, but, but, is there a reason, couldn't you just check all of the partial specializations?
sentences.zh: 所以，但是，但是，有没有什么理由，难道你不能直接检查所有的偏特化吗？

sentences.en: Wouldn't it just be like, like, is there's no way to like exhaustively check?
sentences.zh: 难道不会就像是，就没有办法进行穷举检查吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that trivially exponential?
sentences.zh: 这难道不是显而易见的指数级增长吗？

sentences.en: Um, I suppose so.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想是的。

sentences.en: And there's other constraints here too of, for example, what if you haven't seen the partial specialization at the time you check the template definition?
sentences.zh: 这里也存在其他约束，例如，如果在你检查模板定义时你还没有看到偏特化，那会怎么样？

sentences.en: Do you not consider it at instantiation time or do you admit the failures again?
sentences.zh: 你在实例化时不考虑它，还是再次允许失败？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I, I, I, or I suppose maybe, I suppose like good partial specializations shouldn't, uh, shouldn't different, differ from the primary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我，我，我，或者我想也许，我想好的偏特化不应该，呃，不应该与主模板有差异。

sentences.en: Um, it would just be nice if we had a language way to enforce that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我们有一种语言层面的方式来强制这一点，那就太好了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We could have done that so that, you know, it would be possible to say, okay, the primary template is itself like a concept, right?
sentences.zh: 我们本可以做到这一点，你知道的，这样就可以说，好的，主模板本身就像是一个概念，对吧？

sentences.en: It describes an abstract interface and every specialization, whether partial or full of that template needs to match that interface.
sentences.zh: 它描述了一个抽象接口，该模板的每个特化（无论是偏特化还是全特化）都需要匹配该接口。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That would be completely reasonable direction for the language to take that would help with this kind of problem.
sentences.zh: 这对于语言的发展方向来说是完全合理的，将有助于解决这类问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The other answer is don't allow specialization, which is what Swift does, for example.
sentences.zh: 另一个答案是禁止特化，例如 Swift 就是这么做的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think, I think you probably could have, um, probably could have done that, uh, too.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想，我想你可能也可以，呃，大概也可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, you, you might need different tools, uh, than what C++ has to be able to, to do,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你，你可能需要不同的工具，呃，不同于 C++ 所拥有的工具，才能做到

sentences.en: you know, partial specialization is just one of C++'s mini, you know, uh, janky versions of, uh, of a pattern matching engine.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，偏特化只是 C++ 的众多，呃，蹩脚版本的模式匹配引擎之一。

sentences.en: Um, and there could have been other ways to, to have handled that.
sentences.zh: 呃，可能还有其他方法来处理这个问题。

sentences.en: Um, but we may have had different, may have needed different tools than we would have had.
sentences.zh: 呃，但我们可能需要不同于我们当时拥有的工具。

sentences.en: And, and as you said, so you have the same problem for, for, uh, for an overload set too,
sentences.zh: 而且，正如你所说，所以对于重载集来说，你也遇到了同样的问题，

sentences.en: for, right, for like, uh, uh, yeah, like if you have some, some weird overload that returns
sentences.zh: 对吧，比如，呃，呃，是的，比如如果你有一些返回不同东西的诡异重载，

sentences.en: something different, um, okay, I mean, it's, it's, it's, uh, I, I, I do in, in, I have seen
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的意思是，这，这，呃，我，我，我确实在，在，我见过大量偏特化，它们在某些方面

sentences.en: plenty of, of partial specializations that do something different than the primary in some
sentences.zh: 做的事情与主模板不同，还有重载集，你知道，它们会做一些古怪的事情，通常，通常这主要是实现细节，并不是特别，呃，重要。

sentences.en: way and, and overload sets and which, you know, uh, that do quirky things usually, usually it's mostly implementation details are not particularly, um, uh, important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我确信我能想到一些它确实重要的情况，但我，我，我能理解为什么人们会有这种担忧，并将其与“这种检查不合适”的说法混为一谈。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm sure I can think of some cases where it's mattered, but I, I, I, I could see how people could have that, that concern and could conflate that to claims
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点，或者我，我，我能理解这种说法是如何诞生的，我想可以这么说。

sentences.en: that, uh, that the checking is not, uh, not suitable.
sentences.zh: 我不同意这种说法，但我能理解这种说法是如何产生的。

sentences.en: I think it's a little, or I, I, I can see how that narrative got born, I guess is a way to put it.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't agree with the narrative, but I could see how the narrative got born.
sentences.zh: 我想对此，部分原因在于“完美是优秀的敌人”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I, I think to that, partly this is a, the perfect is the enemy of the good.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 因为对于你编写的绝大多数泛型代码来说，C++0x 概念所拥有的独立类型检查大概都能正常工作。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 而且你从堆栈深处崩溃的东西中获得的绝大多数模板实例化回溯（backtraces）都会消失。

sentences.en: Because for the vast majority of generic code you write, the separate type checking, that C++OX concepts had would probably work.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the vast majority of like template instantiation backtraces that you get from something blowing up deep in the stack would have gone away.
sentences.zh: 因为偏特化，你完全可以做。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我们在某些显而易见的地方使用它们，但你知道，vector<bool> 很显眼，因为它是整个标准库中唯一奇怪的一个。

sentences.en: Because partial specializations, you could do them.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We have them in some obvious places, but you know, vector rule sticks out because it's kind of the only weird one in the entire standard library.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数程序员都不会这样做。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 他们只有一个定义并直接使用它。

sentences.en: And most programmers don't do this.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为其好处将是：常见的模板实例化回溯会变得非常罕见，一旦人们接受了“好吧，我在使用概念，我从中获得了所有这些好处，

sentences.en: They have the one definition and they use it.
sentences.zh: 如果为了在这里做偏特化而不得不放弃这些好处，我会寻找其他方法”这种观念，这种现象可能会变得更加罕见。

sentences.en: And so I think the benefits would have been common template instantiation backtraces would
sentences.zh: 正是这些实例化回溯，才真正构成了我们所拥有的所有问题诊断的根源。

sentences.en: have become a very rare thing, possibly made even rarer once people embrace the notion of, well, I'm using concepts, I'm getting all these benefits from it.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是我的看法。

sentences.en: I would have to give those up to do partial specialization here.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，独立检查本可以消除我们今天所经历的大部分痛苦和折磨。

sentences.en: I'll find another way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你提出了一个很好的观点，即你刚描述的检查的失败模式并不是那种你会得到糟糕的代码或行为诡异的程序的情况。

sentences.en: And it's those instantiation backtraces is really the root of all of the problematic diagnostics that we have.
sentences.zh: 它只是意味着失败发生在编译过程的不同阶段，并且你可能会得到更差的诊断信息，在我看来这非常非常可以接受。

sentences.en: Yes, that's my view.
sentences.zh: 是的，那么 C++11 之后发生了什么？

sentences.en: And the separate checking, I think, would have eliminated much of that pain and suffering that we experience today.
sentences.zh: 听起来，如果我对历史的记忆大致准确的话，并且基于我从 isocpp.org 读给你的那段摘录——

sentences.en: And I mean, you make a good point that the failure mode of the checking that you just described is not one of, you know, you get bad code or a program that does quirky things.
sentences.zh: 对于任何可能有影响力的人来说，那页内容大概需要更新或者删除了，因为它看起来像是 2012 年左右写的，里面谈到的都是已经发生的事情。

sentences.en: It's simply that the failure happens at a different point in the compilation process and that you maybe get a worse diagnostic, which seems very, very tolerable to me.
sentences.zh: 但听起来，不仅是委员会做出了将其从 C++0x 中移除的决定，而且委员会似乎还表态：我们想做点完全不同的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, and so what happened after C++11?
sentences.zh: 他们拒绝了这个设计，而不是像“我们先把它拿掉，以后再回来处理”那样。

sentences.en: So it sounds like, and if I remember the history more or less correctly, and based on the snippet
sentences.zh: 感觉就像是“我们把它拿掉，然后我们要搞这个概念轻量版（concepts light）”。

sentences.en: I read you from isocpp.org, which for anybody who may have influence, that probably needs to
sentences.zh: 这样说大致正确吗？

sentences.en: be updated or that page can be deleted because it seems like it was written in like 2012 and talks about things that have already happened.
sentences.zh: 还是说在 C++0x 之后，真的有人努力推进过 C++0x 模型？

sentences.en: But it sounds like it wasn't just that the decision was made to take it out of C++OX, but that the committee was like, we want to do something different.
sentences.zh: 所以我不认为将其描述为委员会给出了那种方向是合理的。

sentences.en: And that they rejected the design and it wasn't like, we're going to take it out and come back to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，委员会是基于这些担忧才决定将其从 C++0x 中移除的。

sentences.en: It's like, we're going to take it out and we're going to do this concepts light thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为实际发生的情况是，那些极力推动 C++0x 概念的人，比如我自己——我几乎是刚才提到的所有这些论文的第一作者，

sentences.en: Is that more or less correct?
sentences.zh: 在它被移除后，就没有兴趣继续推进它了。

sentences.en: Or was there ever really an effort after C++OX to move forward with the C++OX model?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，从个人历史的角度来看，康纳给出了一个相当准确的近似。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's reasonable to characterize it as the committee giving that level of direction.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，到这个时候，我已经加入苹果公司去开发一个叫 Clang 的东西了，在我加入苹果时，它甚至勉强算是一个没有代码生成的 C 解析器。

sentences.en: You know, the committee decided to remove it from C++OX based on these concerns.
sentences.zh: 我的使命是让它成为一个优秀的 C++ 编译器。

sentences.en: I think what really happened is the people that were pushing for C++OX concepts, like myself, first author on pretty much every one of these papers that I talked about,
sentences.zh: 而这就是我所致力于的工作。

sentences.en: weren't interested in pursuing it further after it got removed.
sentences.zh: 所以我得以实现重载、模板和初始化。

sentences.en: You know, from personal history standpoint, Conor gave a pretty good approximation.
sentences.zh: 以及所有这一切。

sentences.en: But, you know, by this time, I had joined Apple to work on this thing called Clang, which was barely a C parser with no code generation at the time I joined Apple.
sentences.zh: 但回头重新审视 C++0x 概念的想法，在当时并没有多大吸引力。

sentences.en: And my mission was go make it a good C++ compiler.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，仅仅几年后，Clang 就成功了。

sentences.en: And that is what I worked on.
sentences.zh: 我们正在将它推广到苹果的整个生态系统中，谷歌也采用了它并用它做了大量的工作。

sentences.en: So I got to implement overloading and templates and initialization.
sentences.zh: 我们做出了开始开发 Swift 这一新语言的决定。

sentences.en: And everything.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the idea of going back and revisiting C++OX concepts was not terribly appealing at the time.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, just a handful of years later, Clang was succeeding.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某个时候，另一群人开始着手研究概念轻量版模型。

sentences.en: We were rolling it out through Apple's ecosystem and Google picked it up and was doing tons of work with it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那我问你这个。

sentences.en: We made the decision to start working on Swift, a new language.
sentences.zh: 我只是假设你是一个坚定的……

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 投票表决有五种不同的方式。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 我假设你当时是强烈反对将 C++0x 概念从……中移除的。

sentences.en: So at some point, a different group of people started working on the concepts light model.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这样问，是因为有时对于像这样引起巨大争议的特性，作者有时会觉得“好吧，我们确实应该在这上面花更多时间”。

sentences.en: Well, let me ask you this.
sentences.zh: 所以有时答案并不是作者反对这样做。

sentences.en: So I'm just assuming that you were a strong...
sentences.zh: 但我有一种感觉，在这种情况下，不，你是觉得我们本应该把它发布出去的。

sentences.en: There's five different ways of voting on things.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们本应该把它发布出去。

sentences.en: I'm assuming you were a strong against on removing C++OX concepts from...
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the reason I ask is that sometimes with, you know, big controversial features like this, sometimes the authors decide like, yeah, okay, we should take more time on this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常好的模型。

sentences.en: And so sometimes the answer isn't that the author is opposed to this.
sentences.zh: 当时我们用那个模型编写的所有编程工作——在更新各种算法以使用它、

sentences.en: But I had a feeling that in this case, no, you thought we should have shipped it.
sentences.zh: 并试玩 Boost 图形库的概念化（conceptified）版本时——都是非常积极的。

sentences.en: I thought we should have shipped it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常棒的、用起来很舒服的模型。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，我们采用了非常类似于那个模型的东西，它成了 Swift 泛型系统，

sentences.en: I thought it was a very good model.
sentences.zh: 在那里我们得以打磨掉更多的粗糙边缘，这是一个用起来美妙绝伦的模型。

sentences.en: All the programming we have done with that model at the time of updating the various algorithms to use it
sentences.zh: 我认为我们当时就应该把它发布，如果有需要的话，任何问题都可以在日后逐渐解决。

sentences.en: and playing around with like the Boost Graph Library conceptified were very positive.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我强烈反对。

sentences.en: It was a very nice model to work with.
sentences.zh: 我也曾下定决心，如果我投票输了，我就不会再回头搞概念了，尽管在那之后的几年里，

sentences.en: Since then, we took something very much like that model and it became the Swift generic system
sentences.zh: 我作为一名专业的编译器开发人员，依然在全职从事 C++ 的工作。

sentences.en: where we got to clean up even more rough edges and it's a wonderful model to work with.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至可以把更多更难看的边缘情况处理掉，而且用它来写代码真的是妙不可言。

sentences.en: I think we should have shipped it and any issues we could have ironed out over time if that was needed.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们当时就应该把它发布出去，如果有必要的话，任何问题都可以在日后逐渐解决。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I was strongly againSt.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我强烈反对。

sentences.en: I also had decided that if I lost the vote, I wouldn't come back with concepts, even though I was still working on C++, you know, full time as a professional compiler developer
sentences.zh: 我也曾下定决心，如果我投票输了，我就不会再回头搞概念了，尽管在那之后的几年里，

sentences.en: for several years after that.
sentences.zh: 我作为一名专业的编译器开发人员，依然在全职从事 C++ 的工作。

sentences.en: And do you think C++ would have ended up any better positioned if C++ OX concepts had shipped in 11?
sentences.zh: 你觉得如果 C++0X 的 concepts（概念）在 C++11 中发布，C++ 的处境会不会更好一些？

sentences.en: A better position with respect to what?
sentences.zh: 更好是相对于什么而言？

sentences.en: With respect to sort of the next generation systems programming languages and like overall trends of the day and the general...
sentences.zh: 相对于下一代系统编程语言的发展趋势，以及当时的整体潮流和普遍……

sentences.en: You look at C++'s evolution versus other languages and it's maybe not moving quite as faSt.
sentences.zh: 你看 C++ 的演进和其他语言相比，可能发展得没那么快。

sentences.en: It's not, you know, it had this resurgence after C++ 11, but do you think that the landscape of programming languages or the popularity of C++
sentences.zh: 确实没有，你知道的，它在 C++11 之后迎来了复兴，但你认为如果我们在 11 年发布了 concepts，编程语言的格局或 C++ 的普及程度...

sentences.en: would be drastically different today if we'd shipped concepts in 11?
sentences.zh: 今天会不会有天壤之别？

sentences.en: I don't expect it would be drastically different.
sentences.zh: 我倒觉得不会有什么天壤之别。

sentences.en: I mean, I do think that the newer languages have generic systems that were possibly inspired by C++ OX concepts and do a lot of the things that it did well.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的确觉得更新的语言拥有一些泛型系统，可能正是受了 C++0X concepts 的启发，并且很好地实现了它所擅长的许多功能。

sentences.en: Like, it is easier to write generic code in a language that has separate type checking for its generics.
sentences.zh: 比如，在一个对其泛型进行单独类型检查的语言中，编写泛型代码确实更容易。

sentences.en: And a number of languages have proven this out for us.
sentences.zh: 许多语言已经为我们证明了这一点。

sentences.en: In that regard, yes, C++ would have been in a better place.
sentences.zh: 从这个角度来看，是的，C++ 本可以处于一个更好的位置。

sentences.en: But it seems like right now, you know, the concern around C++ is really around memory safety.
sentences.zh: 但眼下看起来，你知道的，围绕 C++ 的担忧主要在于内存安全性。

sentences.en: And concepts would have done nothing there.
sentences.zh: 而 concepts 在这方面起不到任何作用。

sentences.en: Nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 一点作用也没有。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: But I, you know, a lot of the primaries that spent 10 years of their lives or 10 plus years of their lives working on concepts
sentences.zh: 不过我发现，你知道的，许多花了一生中 10 年甚至 10 多年时间来研究 concepts 的核心骨干，

sentences.en: are the same people who are the primaries in the C++ contracts efforts and the same people who are the people who think about safety in C++.
sentences.zh: 恰好也是 C++ contracts（契约）工作中的核心人物，同时也是那些思考 C++ 安全性问题的人。

sentences.en: And so I wonder if concepts had shipped in 11, maybe their efforts would have switched to modules and contracts earlier.
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，如果 concepts 在 11 年发布了，也许他们的精力会更早地转移到模块和契约上。

sentences.en: Maybe we would have gotten something like contracts in a, like, by now.
sentences.zh: 也许我们现在就能得到类似契约这样的特性了。

sentences.en: And maybe C++ would be in a better place.
sentences.zh: 也许 C++ 的处境会更好。

sentences.en: Maybe we would have been better positioned to respond to the growing need for memory safety than we are
sentences.zh: 也许我们能更好地应对日益增长的内存安全需求，而不是像现在这样……

sentences.en: instead of this long redesign effort and then missing 17 and barely making it into 20.
sentences.zh: 经历漫长的重新设计，结果错过了 17 标准，勉强挤进了 20 标准。

sentences.en: This is actually a, it's a, you know, parallel universe mental exercise.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个，这是一个，你知道的，平行宇宙的思想实验。

sentences.en: But it is, I understand what Bryce is saying.
sentences.zh: 但我明白布莱斯（Bryce）的意思。

sentences.en: Like, it's also, you haven't explicitly used these words, but it does seem like out of C++ OX failing to get in.
sentences.zh: 而且，虽然你没有明说，但似乎也正是因为 C++0X 的未能通过……

sentences.en: And I also, on a side thought, on a little tangent, when you were talking about all this, it does strike me as unique to the C++ OX story of being kind of voted out.
sentences.zh: 另外我还有一个题外话，稍微扯远一点，当你谈到这一切时，我确实觉得 C++0X 被投票否决的这段经历非常独特。

sentences.en: I don't know of any other proposal, because there's been others, like contracts that were, you know,
sentences.zh: 我不知道还有什么别的提案——因为确实有其他的，比如契约提案，你知道的，

sentences.en: 11th hour going in and then there was a vote and they weren't, that required an immense amount of work
sentences.zh: 在最后一刻推进，然后进行了一次投票却没有通过，这需要投入巨大数量的工作，

sentences.en: to kind of back out all of these changes that have been made to the standard library.
sentences.zh: 来撤销对标准库所做的一切修改。

sentences.en: Like, I don't know of any other, you know, proposal that necessitated that.
sentences.zh: 总之，我不知道还有哪个提案曾迫使人们这样做。

sentences.en: And I think that that's actually like a unique property to this, is that if it had just been,
sentences.zh: 我觉得这也是它独特的地方，如果当时只是，

sentences.en: okay, we're not going to put this in, but it doesn't necessitate a bunch of work, there's going to be less like fallout.
sentences.zh: “好吧，我们不把这个放进去”，但这不需要大量的工作，那么后续的负面影响就会少一些。

sentences.en: And that kind of ends the tangent to me, adding to what Bryce was saying, is that like, I don't think it was just, I don't want to, you know, throw people's names out there.
sentences.zh: 这就结束了这个题外话。顺着布莱斯的话来说，我觉得这不仅仅是——我不想点名道姓，

sentences.en: But definitely there was more that, it was more than just you, Doug, that left sort of the C++ initiative.
sentences.zh: 但很显然，不仅仅是你，道格（Doug），退出了 C++ 的倡议工作。

sentences.en: And like you said, you were still working on C++, you just didn't have the desire to go and go back to the committee with this.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，你当时仍在从事 C++ 工作，只是不再有那种意愿去把这个带回委员会了。

sentences.en: And then eventually, you know, another opportunity arose with a brand new language that, you know, obviously a colleague of yours, Chris, was working on.
sentences.zh: 后来，你知道的，一个全新的语言带来了新的机遇，显然你的同事克里斯（Chris）当时正在致力于此。

sentences.en: And then, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的……

sentences.en: Dave Abrahams as well joined sort of that.
sentences.zh: 戴夫·亚伯拉罕斯（Dave Abrahams）也加入了进来。

sentences.en: And so then you've got this all-star cast, a lot of who, you know, used to spend a lot of time and energy working on C++.
sentences.zh: 于是你就拥有了一支全明星阵容，其中许多人过去常常花大量时间和精力来开发 C++。

sentences.en: So it is interesting to think, like, what if concepts went in in 11, in the form that they were initially proposed,
sentences.zh: 所以这就很有趣，去思考如果 concepts 在 11 年以最初提出的形式被采纳了会怎样，

sentences.en: a bunch of energy wasn't spent on, you know, the next decade, getting it into C++ 20.
sentences.zh: 大家不用把接下来的十年精力都耗费在把它塞进 C++20 里。

sentences.en: And on top of that, the folks that are now working on other things that used to work on C++, what if they were still there?
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，那些过去从事 C++ 工作现在却在搞别的东西的人，如果他们当时还在呢？

sentences.en: Like the combination of the time and energy spent on extra decade getting concepts in, if that was able to be put towards something else,
sentences.zh: 把花在用十年额外时间引入 concepts 上的时间和精力节省下来，如果能投入到别的事情上去，

sentences.en: and the people that were a part of C++ back then, you know, it's all just gonna like, we don't live in that world.
sentences.zh: 再加上当时参与 C++ 的那些人……这一切，你知道的，我们并不能生活在那个世界里。

sentences.en: So, you know, it's more of a fun exercise than it is actually like, nothing's gonna come of thinking what could have happened in this parallel universe.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，这更多是一个有趣的练习，并没有什么实质意义，去思考在这个平行宇宙中会发生什么也无济于事。

sentences.en: But it's the same thing when I like, what if Bill Gates had implemented, you know, his APL interpreter and
sentences.zh: 这就好比，如果比尔·盖茨当初实现了他的 APL 解释器并，

sentences.en: put it on the PC, we'd be living in this world where, you know, every language was inspired by APL and not basic, you know, we don't live in that world.
sentences.zh: 把它装在 PC 上，我们就会生活在这样一个世界里：所有的语言都是受 APL 而不是 Basic 启发的——你知道的，我们并没有生活在那个世界。

sentences.en: But it is fun to think about what would have happened if that was the decision Bill Gates made.
sentences.zh: 但去思考如果那是比尔·盖茨做出的决定会发生什么，确实很有趣。

sentences.en: Microsoft would have been bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 微软早就破产了。

sentences.en: Sorry, Connor.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，康纳（Connor）。

sentences.en: We'll never know.
sentences.zh: 我们永远不会知道了。

sentences.en: So one of the reasons that I mentioned this hypothetical is, so C++ 11 went long, because it was a feature-based release, not a schedule-based release.
sentences.zh: 我提到这个假设的原因之一是，C++11 拖了很久，因为它是一个基于特性的版本，而不是基于排期的版本。

sentences.en: After C++ 11, you know, famously called C++ OX, because they expected it to ship in the earlier decade.
sentences.zh: C++11 之后，你知道的，它被戏称为 C++0X，因为大家期望它能在更早的十年内发布。

sentences.en: And it was a feature-based release, which means that we said, these are the things we want to ship, and we'll ship the standard when those things are ready.
sentences.zh: 它是一个基于特性的版本，这意味着我们说，这些是我们要发布的特性，当这些特性准备好时，我们就发布标准。

sentences.en: And after that, we moved to a schedule-based release where we shipped every three years.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，我们转向了基于排期的发布模式，每三年发布一次。

sentences.en: And I'll read it.
sentences.zh: 我来读一下。

sentences.en: My reading of that quote from isoCPP.org was very intentional earlier.
sentences.zh: 我刚才对 isoCPP.org 上那段话的解读是非常刻意的。

sentences.en: The last part of that was, and a radically simplified version, Concepts Lite will be part of the C++ 14 wave of deliverables as a technical specification.
sentences.zh: 那句话的最后一部分是：“一个经过根本性简化的版本——Concepts Lite，将作为技术规范成为 C++14 发布浪潮的一部分。”

sentences.en: So after C++ 11, we did a few things.
sentences.zh: 所以在 C++11 之后，我们做了一些事情。

sentences.en: We moved to this schedule-based cycle of releasing every three years, and we got all excited about technical specifications.
sentences.zh: 我们转向了每三年发布一次的排期循环，并且对技术规范（TS）感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And we also, this was the big library era, where we put out a call that we want a giant standard library, everybody come bring your proposals to the committee.
sentences.zh: 而且这也是一个大型标准库的时代，我们发出了号召，想要一个巨大的标准库，欢迎所有人把提案带给委员会。

sentences.en: And that period from like 2011 to 2016 or 17 was sort of like this C++ renaissance, where the committee grew orders of magnitude and size.
sentences.zh: 从 2011 年到 2016 或 2017 年这段时间，有点像 C++ 的文艺复兴时期，委员会的规模呈几个数量级增长。

sentences.en: C++ became very popular because C++ 11 had all these new features in it.
sentences.zh: C++ 变得非常受欢迎，因为 C++11 包含了所有这些新特性。

sentences.en: The committee was inundated with proposals.
sentences.zh: 委员会收到了铺天盖地的提案。

sentences.en: And we started shipping all these technical specifications.
sentences.zh: 我们开始发布所有这些技术规范。

sentences.en: And a lot of good things came out of that era.
sentences.zh: 那个时代确实诞生了很多好东西。

sentences.en: But that era, I think, was also a defining characteristic of that era was unchecked enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 但那个时代，我认为其鲜明的特征也是盲目的热情。

sentences.en: And it was followed by what I like to call the era of small library, which was the post-C++ 17 period where the committee had a two-year backlog on processing
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是我喜欢称之为“小型标准库时代”的时期，也就是 C++17 之后的阶段，当时委员会有两年的积压工作需要处理，

sentences.en: things and features kept missing the boat.
sentences.zh: 各种特性不断错过发布的班车。

sentences.en: And we spent tons of time on technical specifications that we shipped that nobody really implemented.
sentences.zh: 我们花大量时间在那些发布了却无人真正实现的 технически 规范上。

sentences.en: And we never really got the field experience that we wanted from technical specifications.
sentences.zh: 我们从来没有真正从技术规范中获得我们想要的实际经验。

sentences.en: And they just became a way to fast track forcing your thing into the standard.
sentences.zh: 它们最终只是变成了一种强行把你的东西塞进标准的捷径。

sentences.en: And it took us a while after C++ 11 to learn what's the good cadence for us to ship at and how should we prioritize and focus on things.
sentences.zh: C++11 之后，我们花了很长时间才摸索出适合我们的发布节奏，以及如何确定优先级和专注做事。

sentences.en: And I'm not claiming that the committee's figured that out yet, because I still have said many times in this podcast, I don't think we have a good evolution model.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说委员会已经完全搞懂了这一点，因为我在这档播客里已经多次说过，我认为我们还没有一个好的演进模型。

sentences.en: But we certainly have a better evolution model today than we had in that period of time.
sentences.zh: 但今天的演进模型确实比那个时期要好。

sentences.en: And one characteristic of that is that we didn't ship concepts in OX, and then we didn't ship it in 14, and then we didn't ship it in 17, and then we just barely shipped it in 20.
sentences.zh: 其中的一个特征就是：我们在 0X 中没有发布 concepts，在 14 中没有发布，在 17 中也没有发布，直到 20 中才勉强发布。

sentences.en: And that additional decade was really unfortunate for C++.
sentences.zh: 多出来的这十年对 C++ 来说真的很不幸。

sentences.en: I mean, the schedule-based release cycle was really great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基于排期的发布周期真的很棒。

sentences.en: It's been one of the things that has saved C++.
sentences.zh: 这是拯救了 C++ 的伟大举措之一。

sentences.en: One of the great innovations that Herb has brought to the process was that.
sentences.zh: 赫布（Herb）为这个流程带来的伟大创新之一就是这个。

sentences.en: But the period of time that it took for the committee to adapt to that and that sort of unchecked enthusiasm really did hurt us in some ways.
sentences.zh: 但委员会适应这一节奏所花费的时间，以及那种盲目的热情，在某些方面确实伤害了我们。

sentences.en: And I don't think that it needed to take that long to ship it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得发布它并不需要花那么长时间。

sentences.en: Like, I don't think that the concepts needed to go to a TS.
sentences.zh: 比如，我认为 concepts 根本没必要走技术规范（TS）的流程。

sentences.en: I think if, like, we...
sentences.zh: 我想如果，我们……

sentences.en: Concepts lights could have been done and shipped it.
sentences.zh: Concepts lite 完全可以做好并发布。

sentences.en: Like, if we were doing it today, I think we would have done it and shipped it in 14 or 17, and not in 20.
sentences.zh: 如果我们在今天做这件事，我认为我们会在 14 或 17 年就完成并发布它，而不是等到 20 年。

sentences.en: But yeah, it's an interesting hypothetical that, like, as we said before, like, the perfect is the enemy of the good.
sentences.zh: 不过话说回来，这是一个有趣的假设，正如我们之前所说，追求完美是优秀的敌人。

sentences.en: I think C++ would have been far better off if we just shipped OX concepts and moved on to other things, because we had a lot of other work to be doing.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果当初我们直接发布了 OX concepts 然后转向其他事情，C++ 的状况会好得多，因为我们还有很多别的工作要做。

sentences.en: And I also think the feature that we got is so watered down that it doesn't feel like it was worth the energy that we invested in it.
sentences.zh: 而且我也觉得，我们最终得到的特性被严重冲淡了，感觉不值得我们为此投入的精力。

sentences.en: And, like, I guess I would have been willing for the committee to have spent the amount of time that it did on concepts if we'd got something closer to C++ OX concepts.
sentences.zh: 而且，我想如果当初委员会在 concepts 上花费的时间能让我们得到更接近 C++0X concepts 的东西，我是愿意接受的。

sentences.en: But because we got something that doesn't really give me much of what I want, and I think has a syntax that's far harder for me to understand and teach to people,
sentences.zh: 但由于我们得到的成果并不能真正满足我的大部分需求，而且我觉得它的语法对我来说更难理解和向他人传授，

sentences.en: and that makes me just want to avoid the feature other than just as a fancy form of Sfine.
sentences.zh: 这让我只想避开这个特性，除非把它当成 SFINAE 的一种花哨形式。

sentences.en: And I don't get any of the diagnostic or checking benefits out of it.
sentences.zh: 我从它那里根本得不到任何诊断或检查方面的好处。

sentences.en: It doesn't feel like it was a good use of the time.
sentences.zh: 感觉这并不是对时间的合理利用。

sentences.en: And that's unfortunate, because I do think that C++ really could have benefited from a proper generic programming interface.
sentences.zh: 这很遗憾，因为我确实认为 C++ 本可以从一个合适的泛型编程接口中获益良多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't know how many questions were in the last, like, 15 minutes of Bryce, then me, then Bryce, but I feel like we should let Doug
sentences.zh: 我不知道在过去这 15 分钟里——先是布莱斯，然后是我，然后又是布莱斯——到底有多少个问题，但我觉得我们应该让道格……

sentences.en: respond to whatever questions you do recall from the last 15 minutes.
sentences.zh: 来回应你从过去 15 分钟里所记住的任何问题。

sentences.en: I'm not even sure where to pick up the thread here.
sentences.zh: 我都不知道该从哪里切入这个话题了。

sentences.en: So, I certainly agree with you that given all of the time that was spent on concepts, what we got, I think, is a little unfortunate.
sentences.zh: 所以，我完全同意你的看法，考虑到花在 concepts 上的所有时间，我们最终得到的成果确实有点遗憾。

sentences.en: I was rereading the 2003 paper to see what our goals were.
sentences.zh: 我最近重新阅读了 2003 年的论文，想看看我们当时的目标是什么。

sentences.en: And separate type checking is the one goal.
sentences.zh: 独立的类型检查就是其中一个目标。

sentences.en: That is the one thing that if we had it, you could even throw out concept maps.
sentences.zh: 这是唯一的一点，如果我们拥有它，你甚至可以抛弃 concept maps（概念映射）。

sentences.en: If you had separate type checking, it would have made generic programming in C++ an order of magnitude easier.
sentences.zh: 如果你有了独立的类型检查，它会让 C++ 中的泛型编程变得简单一个数量级。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It would no longer be the domain of experts to use templates and use them well.
sentences.zh: 这样使用模板并用好模板就不再是专家们的专属领域了。

sentences.en: It would be something that every programmer just does because they need the abstraction.
sentences.zh: 它将成为每个程序员因为需要抽象而自然而然会去做的事情。

sentences.en: And we have seen it work in other languages.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到它在其他语言中成功了。

sentences.en: And it could have been there in C++.
sentences.zh: 它本可以存在于 C++ 中。

sentences.en: And whether it still can be, I was thinking about this as, can it still be fixed?
sentences.zh: 至于它现在是否还能实现，我一直在思考这个问题：它还能被修复吗？

sentences.en: And it's an interesting question of whether it can.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个有趣的问题，看它是否可行。

sentences.en: So, I did actually write a paper 10 years ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，我其实在 10 年前就写过一篇论文。

sentences.en: It was my last attempt at trying to get separate type checking into concepts light that said, basically, take the concepts and your constraints, generate some
sentences.zh: 那是我最后一次尝试将独立的类型检查引入 concepts lite，其基本思路是：从 concepts 和约束中，生成一些，

sentences.en: archetypes from them, and try to instantiate the template.
sentences.zh: 原型（archetypes），然后尝试实例化模板。

sentences.en: And if it fails, show the error messages.
sentences.zh: 如果失败了，就显示错误信息。

sentences.en: So that the, I don't know, this archetypes thing came out of a boost, boost concept checked library.
sentences.zh: 这样，这个原型机制——我不知道，这个原型概念源自 Boost 的 concept check 库。

sentences.en: I should explain it.
sentences.zh: 我应该解释一下。

sentences.en: I was about to say, because there were two, there were two things that we haven't covered yet.
sentences.zh: 我正要说呢，因为还有两个我们尚未涵盖的内容。

sentences.en: And it was archetypes in axioMs. And maybe archetypes is a good thing to start with.
sentences.zh: 那就是 axioms（公理）中的原型，也许从原型开始讲是个不错的主意。

sentences.en: Archetypes is a good one.
sentences.zh: 原型确实是个好切入点。

sentences.en: So an archetype is essentially a fresh concrete type.
sentences.zh: 所以，一个原型本质上是一个全新的具体类型。

sentences.en: And the only operations that are on that concrete type are the operations that are explained by the concept requirements for it.
sentences.zh: 在这个具体类型上仅有的操作，就是由其 concept 需求所解释的操作。

sentences.en: So if you were to say, hey, I have an algorithm that takes an arbitrary container and that element is equatable.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你说，嘿，我有一个算法，它接受一个任意容器，并且该容器的元素是可比较相等的（equatable）。

sentences.en: Now, you could create an archetype for the container that is just a plain old class, has no state, has no operations, other than what the container type says it needs.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以为该容器创建一个原型，它只是一个普通的类，没有状态，也没有任何操作，除了容器类型声明它所需要的功能外什么都没有。

sentences.en: So it needs to have a begin and an end, maybe, right?
sentences.zh: 所以它需要有 begin 和 end，也许吧？

sentences.en: Let's keep this simple.
sentences.zh: 我们把问题保持简单。

sentences.en: So it has begin and end.
sentences.zh: 所以它有 begin 和 end。

sentences.en: Those return iterators.
sentences.zh: 这些方法会返回迭代器。

sentences.en: It creates a fresh archetype for an iterator.
sentences.zh: 它会为迭代器创建一个全新的原型。

sentences.en: What's that?
sentences.zh: 那是什么？

sentences.en: Well, it has the dereference operator, the plus plus operator.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它拥有解引用运算符、自增运算符。

sentences.en: It's equatable.
sentences.zh: 它是可判等的。

sentences.en: And so you build this little set of types that are completely minimal.
sentences.zh: 于是你构建了这样一小套完全极简的类型。

sentences.en: They only match the requirements that are placed in the requires clause for that one specific constraint template.
sentences.zh: 它们仅匹配针对该特定约束模板的 requires 子句中提出的要求。

sentences.en: Now, then you go try to instantiate the template with those archetypes.
sentences.zh: 然后，你就可以尝试用这些原型去实例化模板。

sentences.en: If your template definition is good, if it's only using the operations that are specified in your requirements, and it's only
sentences.zh: 如果你的模板定义是好的，如果它只使用了你的需求中指定的操作，并且只，

sentences.en: calling into other templates that have the same set of requirements or a subset of them, then your instantiation will succeed.
sentences.zh: 调用了具有相同或子集要求的其他模板，那么你的实例化就会成功。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: You have now separately type checked your template definition.
sentences.zh: 你现在已经对你的模板定义进行了独立的类型检查。

sentences.en: The reason I propose this is it is a reasonable simplification to the C++ OX model.
sentences.zh: 我提出这个方案的原因是，它是对 C++0X 模型的一种合理简化。

sentences.en: It takes away all of the nice things that you get out of concept maps, for sure.
sentences.zh: 它确实剥离了你能从 concept maps 中获得的所有美好特性。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You can no longer do cool remapping syntax to say,
sentences.zh: 你不能再使用酷炫的重新映射语法来说，

sentences.en: Ooh, you know, I can, I can make the matrix type from this library work as a graph type for this library, right?
sentences.zh: 哦，你知道的，我可以让这个库中的矩阵类型作为这个库中的图类型工作，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is my favorite example of cool things you can do with concept maps.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的关于 concept maps 用途酷炫的例子。

sentences.en: You don't get to do any of the fancy things, but you get separate type checking.
sentences.zh: 你无法做任何这些花哨的事情，但你得到了独立的类型检查。

sentences.en: You get the simplification that comes from having separate type checking.
sentences.zh: 你得到了伴随独立类型检查而来的简化。

sentences.en: And it's a lot easier to specify and implement because all you have to say is how do I map the requirements of my concept over to an archetype?
sentences.zh: 而且它更容易规范和实现，因为你只需要说明如何将 concept 的需求映射到一个原型上。

sentences.en: And that's a mechanical translation.
sentences.zh: 而这是一种机械翻译。

sentences.en: It's a little easier with pseudo signatures than it is with usage patterns, but like we could define what it means for usage patterns.
sentences.zh: 使用伪签名比使用使用模式要稍微容易一些，不过我们可以定义使用模式意味着什么。

sentences.en: So maybe that model, maybe you could retrofit that.
sentences.zh: 所以也许那个模型，也许你可以对它进行改造。

sentences.en: It's hard.
sentences.zh: 这很难。

sentences.en: You would break all the code that has concepts now, because I guarantee you nearly all of it has some subtle bug, right?
sentences.zh: 你会破坏所有现在包含概念的代码，因为我向你保证，其中几乎所有代码都包含一些微妙的错误，对吧？

sentences.en: Every template definition that has a concept constraint on it has a subtle bug, but you could possibly get to that model where you have
sentences.zh: 每一个带有概念约束的模板定义都包含一个微妙的错误，但你可能最终会得到这样一个模型：

sentences.en: separate type checking in a, in a much more limited form.
sentences.zh: 以一种更受限制的形式在某个地方进行独立的类型检查。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Sadly, I think that, that ship has sailed.
sentences.zh: 可口的是，我认为那艘船已经开走了。

sentences.en: Um, but, uh, oh, axioms, you should, uh, you should explain the axioMs.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但是，哦，公理，你应该，呃，你应该解释一下公理。

sentences.en: AxioMs. Yes.
sentences.zh: 公理。是的。

sentences.en: Uh, axioms were a feature in the C++OX concepts design that essentially the idea was you could describe semantic constraints on your concepts.
sentences.zh: 呃，公理是 C++OX 概念设计中的一个特性，其基本思想是你可以描述你的概念上的语义约束。

sentences.en: And so this might be things like, for example, uh, if you have an equatable concept, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是这样的事情，例如，呃，如果你有一个可比较的概念，对吧？

sentences.en: It lets you just compare two Ts and say whether they're equal, you would have an axiom inside that concept that said, well, if you have a value X,
sentences.zh: 它让你只比较两个 T 并说明它们是否相等，你会在该概念中有一个公理，即，如果你有一个值 X，

sentences.en: X is equal to X.
sentences.zh: X 等于 X。

sentences.en: And if you have two values, X and Y, then X equal, equal Y is equivalent to Y equals, equals X, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你有两个值 X 和 Y，那么 X 等于 Y 等价于 Y 等于 X，对吧？

sentences.en: The standard, standard properties you'd expect.
sentences.zh: 标准，你所期望的标准属性。

sentences.en: You also have the transitive property that's, you know, X is Y and Y is Z.
sentences.zh: 你还有传递性，你知道的，X 是 Y，Y 是 Z。

sentences.en: Therefore, X is equal to Z.
sentences.zh: 因此，X 等于 Z。

sentences.en: And in C++OX concepts, you could actually write axiom.
sentences.zh: 在 C++OX 概念中，你实际上可以编写公理。

sentences.en: It was a new keyword and write out these semantic properties.
sentences.zh: 这是一个新的关键字，用来写出这些语义属性。

sentences.en: The, the idea and the hope behind, uh, axioms is that this would provide valuable information to
sentences.zh: 呃，公理背后的想法和希望是，这将为以下方面提供有价值的信息：

sentences.en: both users to understand like what their types need to do to actually conform to the concept
sentences.zh: 一方面是让用户理解他们的类型需要做什么才能实际符合该概念，

sentences.en: and that it could be used by static checkers and optimizers and so on to, to go and make sure that
sentences.zh: 另一方面它可以被静态检查器和优化器等使用，去确保

sentences.en: the thing code was more correct or to improve performance by letting you do high level optimizations.
sentences.zh: 代码更加正确，或者通过让你进行高级优化来提高性能。

sentences.en: It was almost, uh, uh, in the family of things that contracts might be in.
sentences.zh: 它几乎，呃，呃，属于契约可能所属的那一类东西。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Cause one, one perhaps important thing that, that, uh, wasn't captured.
sentences.zh: 因为有一个，也许很重要的事情，呃，没有被捕获到。

sentences.en: I don't know if we've captured thus far as the, that, um, concepts have both syntactic and semantic requirements.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们到目前为止是否捕获了这一点，即，呃，概念既有句法要求，也有语义要求。

sentences.en: And the language feature that we have today can only check the syntactic requirements, but that does not mean that the semantic requirements are not important.
sentences.zh: 我们今天拥有的语言特性只能检查句法要求，但这并不意味着语义要求不重要。

sentences.en: Like we talked a little bit before about like, you know, the, the view concept is something that has, uh, semantic requirements that are very important.
sentences.zh: 就像我们之前稍微讨论过的，你知道的，view（视图）概念具有非常重要的语义要求。

sentences.en: Like that.
sentences.zh: 就像那样。

sentences.en: It has O one, uh, you know, uh, copying, um, and a bunch of other operations have important, uh, complexity requirements, um, that essentially mean that these things are cheap
sentences.zh: 它具有 O(1) 的，你知道的，复制操作，以及一堆其他操作，它们具有重要的复杂度要求，呃，这基本上意味着这些东西

sentences.en: to copy around and to pass around.
sentences.zh: 复制和传递的成本很低。

sentences.en: Um, and that's what, like, that's what distinguishes a view from a range.
sentences.zh: 呃，这就是，这就是视图和范围（range）的区别所在。

sentences.en: And that's not something that we can syntactically, um, uh, uh, uh, distinguish.
sentences.zh: 这不是我们通过句法能够，呃，呃，区分出来的。

sentences.en: And that's why, um, like you have to opt in your, your range is to opt into being a view using some trait.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么，呃，就像你必须让你的范围使用某种特征（trait）来显式选择成为一个视图。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, I, I do, it does amuse me the, how frequently I see people having to define C++ 20
sentences.zh: 呃，是的，我，我确实觉得很有趣，我经常看到人们不得不去定义 C++ 20

sentences.en: concepts, um, using some trait mechanism or, uh, just using like, uh, the new things like alias templates.
sentences.zh: 概念，呃，使用某种特征机制，或者，呃，仅仅使用像别名模板这样新东西。

sentences.en: There's a bunch of, I just saw a talk the other day by Gaspar where he was showing some trick using some alias templates to define a concept or the concepts that have to be
sentences.zh: 有一堆，我前几天刚看到 Gaspar 的一个演讲，他在其中展示了一些技巧，使用一些别名模板来定义一个概念，或者那些必须

sentences.en: defined in terms of type traits.
sentences.zh: 根据类型特征来定义的概念。

sentences.en: Um, uh, surely a, a true sign of our success.
sentences.zh: 呃，这无疑是我们成功的一个真正的标志。

sentences.en: Traits have been used since the early STL as the way to opt into behavior and state, you know, this is what concept maps did.
sentences.zh: 从早期的 STL 开始，特征就被用作选择行为和状态的方式，你知道的，这就是概念映射（concept maps）所做的事情。

sentences.en: You can think of concept maps as essentially formalizing the notion of traits with some bells and whistles and actual language integration rather than being a
sentences.zh: 你可以将概念映射本质上视为将特征的概念正式化，并带有一些附加功能和实际的语言集成，而不是基于

sentences.en: specialization based template trick.
sentences.zh: 特化的模板技巧。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: And so, so for anybody who might be thinking like, oh, this concept map thing sounds heavy handed.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于任何可能认为“哦，这个概念映射听起来很笨重”的人来说。

sentences.en: Like, I don't have to want to like, like with the concepts we have, we don't have to explicitly opt into, um, to things.
sentences.zh: 就像，我不一定想要像我们拥有的概念那样，我们不必显式地选择，呃，某些事情。

sentences.en: Well, you know, you look at how many concepts are written in a lot of libraries.
sentences.zh: 好吧，你看，在许多库中编写了多少概念。

sentences.en: There are still a lot of cases where you have to explicitly opt into something.
sentences.zh: 仍然有很多情况下你必须显式地选择某些东西。

sentences.en: There's just no formalized way to do it.
sentences.zh: 只是没有一种形式化的方法来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Concepts maps would have given us that.
sentences.zh: 概念映射本来可以给我们提供这一点。

sentences.en: And with the auto concepts, uh, you would have gotten all of the implicitness that you want.
sentences.zh: 有了自动概念（auto concepts），呃，你就会得到你想要的所有隐式性。
